title: Electromagnetically transparent wall: two slabs with tilted optic axes
source: Z. L. Mei, Y. L. Xu, J. Bai, T. J. Cui, Opt. Express 20, 16955-16967 (2012), Eqs. 3, 8-14 and 18
notes: Each slab has principal values K and 1/K (K = 5.8341, Eq. 18) in the plane of incidence, with eps_zz = 1 in this program's axes (z normal to the slab; the paper's x). Then eps_xx = 1 + c^2 and eps_xz = c with c = (K - 1)/sqrt(K), and the p (TM) block of Delta is the vacuum one plus -xi c times the identity: no reflection at any angle, and a transmitted phase k0 d (cos(theta) - c sin(theta)). The two slabs have opposite c, so the pair transmits exactly as the same thickness of vacuum. Eq. 18b as printed gives slab 2 the same sign of eps_xz as slab 1, which contradicts the paper's own Eqs. 9-14; the consistent sign is used here. eps_yy is not given and does not affect p; it is set to 1. d1 = d2 = 0.44 um at 365 nm (Eq. 18).
